newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL OVERNIGHT RATE RISES DESPITE BANK LENDING.
newsitem.headline: KL OVERNIGHT RATE RISES DESPITE BANK LENDING.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to a high of 6.5/6 percent from 5.5 percent on Wednesday despite continued lending by foreign banks long on ringgit, dealers said on Thursday.
At 0830 GMT, the overnight was quoted at 6.2/3 percent.
"Foreign banks are still lending on the overnight but at higher rates," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the banks were also seen lending one-week and one-month money on Thursday morning.
The market has been short of ringgit as a result of Bank Negara's mopping up of 6-8 billion ringgit in various interventions over the last couple of months, coupled with the flight of foreign funds.
"Foreigners are long and with ringgit still weak, the only option is for them to lend out the money," the dealer said.
Earlier, interbank rates were lower following the sharp drop in the overnight rate on Wednesday.
One-week money was at 7.5 percent against 8.0 percent on Wednesday.
One-month money was at 7.8/8.0 percent from 8.1/2 percent, while three-month was at 7.9/8.0 percent against 8.0/1 percent.
Dealers said interbank rates were expected to come off further due to maturity of Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit on Friday.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were little changed in thin trading.
At 0830 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down one point to 92.43, or an implied yield of 7.57 percent.
The December contract was unchanged at 92.64, or 7.36 percent.
